data.name: AutoStart_ConfirmMessage
data.value:
GlassMonitor will start automatically when you sign in to Windows.
Because reading the sensors requires administrator rights, a task named "{0}" is registered in Task Scheduler to run with highest privileges. No UAC prompt appears at sign-in.
You can turn this off in the settings at any time. Turn it off before you move or delete the app folder.
data.comment: {0} = task name (GlassMonitor). "Run with highest privileges" is the option name in Task Scheduler.

data.name: AutoStart_TaskDescription

data.comment: Description of the task shown in Task Scheduler.

data.name: PawnIo_NotInstalled
data.comment: Shown at the bottom of the settings panel: "PawnIO not installed".

data.name: PawnIo_DescriptionNotInstalled
data.value: GlassMonitor uses PawnIO, an open-source driver, to read CPU temperature, clock and power and motherboard fan speeds. Without PawnIO, GlassMonitor runs in CPU sensor limited mode and these values are shown as "—". GPU, memory and storage are shown as usual.

data.name: PawnIo_DescriptionUnavailable
data.value: PawnIO is installed, but the CPU sensors could not be read. This happens when an anti-cheat such as FACEIT blocks PawnIO or when the driver is not loaded. GlassMonitor runs in CPU sensor limited mode, and CPU temperature, clock, power and fan speeds are shown as "—". GPU, memory and storage are shown as usual.

data.name: PawnIo_FirstStepNotInstalled
data.value: 1. Download PawnIO_setup.exe from the official site or the GitHub releases and run it.

data.name: PawnIo_FirstStepUnavailable
data.value: 1. If you use an anti-cheat such as FACEIT, exit it and restart your PC. If that does not help, reinstall PawnIO from the official site or the GitHub releases.

data.name: PawnIo_WingetHintNotInstalled
data.value: To use winget, run the following command in a terminal.

data.name: PawnIo_WingetHintUnavailable
data.value: With winget, you can update to the latest version with the following command.

data.name: PawnIo_LastStepUnavailable
data.value: 2. When you are done, restart GlassMonitor.
